newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin's Chubais sees only brief power transfer.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin's Chubais sees only brief power transfer.

text.p: Anatoly Chubais, Boris Yeltsin's chief aide, said on Saturday there was no need for the Russian president to hand over power right now although he could put his prime minister in charge briefly while he had a heart operation.
Itar-Tass and Interfax news agencies quoted Chubais as saying Yeltsin was in "normal working condition" despite announcing this week that he would undergo heart surgery at the end of the month.
"So there are no grounds for raising the question of handing over the presidential powers (now)," Tass said.
On Friday, Kremlin security chief Alexander Lebed said Yeltsin should waste no time in handing over power to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, his constitutional deputy.
Chubais, Chernomyrdin and Lebed are widely seen as a triumvirate of rivals jostling for influence around Yeltsin.

Tass quoted Chubais as saying: "If the operation which the president spoke about actually takes place, then I do not rule out that the powers of the head of state could be temporarily transferred to the prime minister, in line with the constitution."
But Interfax quoted Chubais as adding that Chernomyrdin might take power only for a very short time at most: "It would be for a matter of hours, days, a couple of days."
He said that Yeltsin, only holiday at the Rus hunting lodge near Moscow, might soon meet Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov.
Many observers see Luzhkov, who has close links to Moscow's wealthy business community, as a key power broker who could some day also seek the presidency himself.
